name: treesum-arms
description: W1-a (E2, greenfield): treesum — the arms' bundle for B `aisef` and C `aisef+`. Four stories; every contract tests an example the public task text gives (docs/requirements.md); nothing of the hidden evaluator is here.

requirements.text: treesum uses the Python standard library only: no third-party dependency exists and none may be added.
treesum.digest.file_sha256(path) returns the SHA-256 of the file's bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
path may be a str or a pathlib.Path. A path that does not exist raises FileNotFoundError.
treesum.snapshot.build(root) returns a dict mapping every file under root, recursively, to its file_sha256, keyed by the path relative to root with / as separator.
A root that does not exist, or that exists and is not a directory, raises NotADirectoryError.
treesum.snapshot.dumps(snapshot) returns one line per entry, `<sha256>  <path>`, each ended by a newline, in ascending order of path.

treesum.snapshot.loads(text) parses the snapshot text format back into a dict. Empty lines and lines holding only whitespace are ignored; a final line without a newline is read like any other. A line that is not <64 lowercase hex characters>, two spaces, <a non-empty path> raises ValueError.
loads(dumps(s)) == s for every snapshot s.
treesum.snapshot.compare(old, new) returns a dict with exactly the keys added, removed and changed, each a list of paths in ascending order.
python -m treesum build DIR writes dumps(build(DIR)) to standard output and exits 0.

python -m treesum build DIR -o FILE writes the same text to FILE instead — creating it, or replacing its previous content — with nothing on standard output, and exits 0. When FILE lies inside DIR, FILE is not an entry of the snapshot.
python -m treesum verify DIR FILE prints one line per difference and exits 0 when there is no difference, 1 when there is at least one.

Any other use exits 2 with a message on standard error and nothing on standard output: an unknown or missing subcommand, missing or extra arguments, a DIR that is not a directory, a FILE that cannot be read or that does not parse.

contracts.rationale: the example of 1.1: the six bytes `hello\n`
two files in a flat directory: each key is the relative path, each value its digest
the example of 3.1, handed in the reverse order: the text is sorted by path
the example text of 3.1 parses back into its snapshot (3.3)
one added, one changed, nothing removed: the empty list is still present (4.1)
5.2 on the two-file directory of BC-BUILD: the text of 3.1 on standard output, exit 0
5.4 with a snapshot that matches the directory: nothing printed, exit 0
no import statement of the package names a module outside the standard library (preamble)
1.2 on the simplest input: a path (a str) that does not exist raises FileNotFoundError
2.3 on the simplest input: a root that does not exist raises NotADirectoryError
3.3 on one snapshot s of three entries (one nested path): the text is dumps(s) by 3.1, and loads of it is s
5.3 on the two-file directory of BC-BUILD: FILE holds the text of 3.1, exit 0
5.5 on the simplest misuse: python -m treesum with no arguments (a missing subcommand) exits 2
